d: The part of the prostate that surrounds the urethra just below the bladder. It is the only zone that develops benign prostatic hyperplasia, which is why overgrowth squeezes the urethra early and causes urinary symptoms.
The posterior and lateral part of the prostate, about 70% of the gland. It lies against the rectum, so a hard nodule is felt on rectal exam, and it is where 70 to 80% of prostate cancers begin.

A potent androgen made from testosterone by 5-alpha-reductase in the prostate, seminal vesicles and genital skin. It binds the androgen receptor more tightly than testosterone and drives prostate growth, so BPH needs it.

Prostate-specific antigen, a protease made by prostate epithelium that liquefies semen. It is organ-specific, not cancer-specific, so BPH, prostatitis, instrumentation and ejaculation raise it, while 5-alpha-reductase inhibitors halve it.

The flat cell layer under the secretory cells of normal prostate glands, shown by p63 and high-molecular-weight keratin stains. Its absence in small crowded glands is the key histologic criterion for prostate adenocarcinoma.

The tough, inelastic fibrous sheath around the corpora cavernosa. It traps blood during erection, scars into a plaque in Peyronie disease, and can rupture in penile fracture when the erect penis is bent.
